newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia waits for word from Bre-X, Barrick.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia waits for word from Bre-X, Barrick.

text.p: A senior Indonesian mines official said on Wednesday there had been no deal yet between Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp over the spectacular Busang gold find in East Kalimantan.

Umar Said, secretary-general of the Mines Department, said the government had given the two companies, both Canadian, until Wednesday to strike a partnership deal or else it would explore other possibilities in developing the find.
He did not specify when on Wednesday the deadline expired.
"If they cannot reach an agreement, the government will take the necessary and appropriate action...to expedite the development of Busang's resources," he told a news conference.
"What the action will be...I have to get back to the government. This is not my playground."

The government gave Bre-X and Barrick the Wednesday deadline to strike an agreement on exploiting Busang, estimated by Bre-X in an upwardly revised calculation on Tuesday to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
The government has advised that Barrick take a 75 percent stake in the project, with Bre-X holding the rest, and has asked both parties to allocate the government a 10 percent stake.

Barrick has teamed up with a construction company in the Citra Group of President Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, in what Barrick had said was a partnership "to prepare us for a potential mining development project".

Bre-X has said it had a partnership deal with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group run by Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, under which Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent stake in Busang's richest areas.
Umar said the government had not interfered in Busang and had merely helped to "bridge" the gap between Bre-X and Barrick.
"No one can find any traces that the government had interfered in any general mining project. If there are problems, we try to bridge the parties concerned," he said.
"It is in our national interest that resources under our ground should be developed as soon as possible.
"If someone has a mining right under a contract of work and he has found something, it is legal to develop (the find) further."
Umar said Bre-X did not have a contract of work for the richest parts of Busang and that it had not informed the Mines and Energy Ministry of its find.

"Why didn't they report to the government (on their find)," he said, adding that applications for contracts of work by Bre-X were not among those currently awaiting final approval from President Suharto.

Umar also said that a contract of work was issued to PT WAM (Westralian Atan Minerals) for the central section of Busang, in which two Indonesian companies each had a 10 percent stake, with the rest being held by Westralian Resources Project Ltd.
He said that in 1993, Westralian sold its stake to Montague Pacific but the transaction was not reported to the government.
"Montague then sold its shares to Bre-X and this, too, was not reported to us," he said. "This is the true story."
He said Barrick was selected by the government to partner Bre-X because of its high rating by the global mining community.
On the proposed 10-percent stake to be allocated to the government, Umar said: "If they want to give, why do we need to cause problems."
